title: " Correspondances " fonctorielles. Dualité des topos : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A is a (small) category, A^ = presheaves [A^op,Set], A^v = copresheaves [A,Set]. The previous page set up the pairing <Φ_*,Ψ^*>_A between A^ and A^v (the coend/tensor product Φ ⊗_A Ψ) and the adjunction formulas for f_!, f^*, f°_!, f°*.

This page has two steps.

(1) Restrictions of an object of an ambient category. Let A ⊂ B be a fully faithful inclusion and x ∈ B. Define H_x ∈ A^ by H_x(a) = Hom_B(a,x), and H^x ∈ A^v by H^x(b) = Hom_B(x,b). Composition gives a map α_x : H_x(a) × H^x(b) → Hom_B(a,b) = Hom_A(a,b), (u,v) ↦ v∘u. The last identification uses full faithfulness, and α_x is natural in both a and b.

(2) The category Ã of triples. Abstracting from (1), Ã has as objects the triples (H_*, H^*, α), where:
- H_* ∈ A^ and H^* ∈ A^v;
- α : H_*(a) × H^*(b) → Hom_A(a,b) is natural in a and b. Equivalently, α is a map of profunctors H_* ⊠ H^* ⇒ Hom_A.

A morphism (H_*,H^*,α) → (H'_*,H'^*,α') is a pair consisting of φ_* : H_* → H'_* in A^ and φ^* : H'^* → H^* in A^v (note the reversed direction). The pair must satisfy α(u, φ^*(v')) = α'(φ_*(u), v') for u ∈ H_*(a) and v' ∈ H'^*(b). The margin diagram (a →u x → x' →v' b) checks this against the model case: a map x → x' in B induces such a pair, by associativity of composition.

For a fully faithful functor φ : A → B one gets a canonical functor φ^~ : B → Ã, x ↦ (φ^*(h_x), φ°*(h^x), α_x), restricting representables along φ.

In modern terms Ã is exactly the Isbell envelope of A: the full subcategory of the 'collage' of the Isbell adjunction A^ ⇄ (A^v)^op. A triple (F,G,α) is the same as a map G → F^♮ in A^v, or equivalently F → G^♭ in A^. B → Ã is the comparison from any fully faithful extension of A into its envelope.

The next page develops further points:
- self-duality Ã^op ≅ (A^op)~;
- the embeddings A^ ↪ Ã ↩ (A^v)^op, F ↦ (F, F^♮, α_F) and G ↦ (G^♭, G, α_G), i.e. Isbell conjugation;
- the intersection of these two essential images, which is the reflexive completion (Isbell fixed points);
- contravariant functoriality f^~ : B̃ → Ã compatible with f^* and f°*.

The page thus serves Grothendieck's project of 'correspondances fonctorielles' and a duality for topoi: a single category containing both presheaves and (opposite) copresheaves, glued along Hom_A.
errors: H^x should be defined as H^x(b) = Hom_B(x,b) (covariant in b). As written/transcribed it reads Hom_B(a,x), a slip of notation.
In the compatibility equation the map applied to v' is written φ'_*; it should be φ^* : H'^* → H^*.
In the final line the notation φ^*(x), φ°*(x) abbreviates φ^*(h_x) and φ°*(h^x); the target is written A^~ / Ã inconsistently. These are notational, not mathematical, issues.
Full faithfulness is needed only to identify Hom_B(a,b) with Hom_A(a,b). For a merely arbitrary φ one would compose with Hom_B(φa,φb) and need a map back, so the hypothesis is used correctly.

ideas.what: Category of triples (presheaf F, copresheaf G, natural pairing F(a)×G(b)→Hom_A(a,b)), with morphisms covariant in F and contravariant in G
ideas.modern_name: Isbell envelope (collage of the Isbell conjugacy adjunction)
ideas.usually_credited_to: J. Isbell (1960s); modern treatments by R. Garner, 'The Isbell monad' (2015), and Avery–Leinster, 'Isbell conjugacy and the reflexive completion' (2021)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA; possibly related remarks in Pursuing Stacks/Dérivateurs period, unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently reconstructed the Isbell envelope around 1982+, together with its self-duality, the Isbell conjugates F^♮/G^♭ and its contravariant functoriality (next page). He did so explicitly in the context of a 'dualité des topos'. This rediscovery is not recorded in the historical literature on Isbell duality.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit; also documents that Grothendieck saw Isbell-type constructions as a route to topos duality, decades before the Garner/Avery–Leinster revival.

missed.claim: Links the Isbell envelope / reflexive completion with the duality of topoi (presheaf topos A^ versus the copresheaf side A^v) and with functoriality along f : A → B via f^*, f°* and f_!, f°_!.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modern work treats Isbell duality mostly at the level of small categories and enriched settings. A topos-theoretic duality built on the envelope, compatible with geometric-morphism functoriality, is a thread that seems not systematically developed.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction itself is the known Isbell envelope, so mathematically it is not new. The independent rediscovery by Grothendieck, explicitly aimed at duality of topoi, is a modest but genuine historical detail not in the record.
transcription_corrections: H^x(a) = Hom_B(a,x) should read H^x(b) = Hom_B(x,b) (likely Grothendieck's slip or a misreading; context requires covariance).
'tels que {+le diagramme suivant soit [?]+}' : the image reads roughly 'tels que [le diagramme] soit [commutatif]' with an inserted word above ('le diagramme'/'commute'); uncertain.
In the equation α_{a,b}(u, φ'_*(v')), the symbol is φ^* (the upward arrow in the diagram).
Final line: 'φ^~ : B → A^~, x ↦ (φ^*(x), φ°*(x), α_x)'; the functor is named with the letter of the given functor (written like 'f'/'φ').
